newsitem.title: CANADA: Placer Pipeline mill starts early.
newsitem.headline: Placer Pipeline mill starts early.

text.p: Placer Dome Inc commissioned new gold processing facilities for the Pipeline mine in Nevada on Thursday, three months ahead of schedule.
The deposit is at Placer's 60-percent owned Cortez joint venture. RTZ Corp Plc unit Kennecott is Placer's partner in the venture.

Placer said the facility, where the first gold dore was poured on Thursday, was completed at a cost of US$250 million, about US$70 million under budget. The estimated average life-of-mine cash production cost was lowered to US$135 an ounce from US$152. The cost estimate was lowered based on expectations for increased production and revised mining and de-watering costs.
The facilities are expected to enter commercial production before the end of March.

The long-awaited mill is the second at the joint venture. Placer said it expects its share of the combined Cortez-Pipline production is budgeted to be more than 200,000 ounces of gold in 1997 at a cost under US$200 an ounce.
